novelty_flags.label: Proposition 1 (nonrectangular witness)
novelty_flags.one_line: The proposition claims that “coordinatewise or statewise imputation bounds followed by generic optimal transport are not sharp” but identifies no published estimator or workflow that actually uses that sequential procedure.

novelty_flags.label: related_work / flagship sharpness theorem
novelty_flags.one_line: Add and distinguish HuangFangHanleyRosenblum2019, a materially closer randomized-trial fraction-benefiting comparator, rather than leaving it only in the bibliography and seed history.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The preprint states that sharp identified sets for moments of the joint potential-outcome distribution are intervals with optimal-transport endpoint values, and proposes root-n estimators and bootstrap inference.
The paper gives model-agnostic optimal-transport-duality inference for a wide class of partially identified causal estimands, including randomized experiments with discrete or continuous outcomes.

source_verification_receipts.version: Biometrics 82(1), ujag030; PMC author manuscript identifying final edited publication
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper develops doubly robust estimation for average treatment effects in CRTs with missing outcomes, incomplete covariates, and informative cluster sizes, plus a CRT sensitivity-analysis framework.
The paper introduces a self-censoring model for multivariate nonmonotone missing data and identifies the full-data law under its completeness condition.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of the American Statistical Association 119(548), 2024
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article studies cluster- and individual-average CRT effects with variable cluster sizes and uses bounded source-population size in its asymptotic framework.
The paper studies confidence intervals for the partially identified fraction who benefit from treatment in randomized trials with ordinal or binary outcomes.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Name a published sequential completion-plus-transport workflow, state its precise algorithm, and show that the witness violates its claimed sharpness; otherwise present the witness only as an internal nonrectangularity diagnostic.
Add HuangFangHanleyRosenblum2019 to related work and state exactly how vector strict-Pareto benefit with response-pattern selection differs from its ordinal/binary fraction-benefiting target.

Elevate the certificate OEQ into a concrete finite pattern family with either a proved min-cut reduction or a non-representability theorem, so the project has an advance beyond finite-LP sharpness and generic duality.

recommended_next_step: Revise the witness into a comparison against a named published workflow and repair the missing fraction-benefiting literature comparison; the joint missing-state/cross-world sharpness kernel otherwise remains field-plausible.
